start_record.expected_result: Reuse a user-authorized Codex login from private writable App Server state so opening the Tailnet page after service or host restart goes directly to Codex.

observations.scope_boundary: This task persists one user-authorized Codex login only. It does not add or switch accounts, claim cross-account continuity, expose port 8214 publicly, or place credentials in the repository.
observations.result: The real account credential is isolated to the router. App Server and codex-web use a separate router-managed local identity, so fresh pages open the Codex composer without a ChatGPT sign-in prompt.
observations.verification: The corrected account/read result reported an account, a fresh page rendered New task, the composer and Settings, and the same checks passed after independently restarting App Server and codex-web.
observations.deployment: The existing M6.5 Tailnet release remains active. All three services are active, health is 200, the router-managed marker files are private and separated from the real Primary credential, and temporary authorization artifacts were removed.

residual_risks: Every Tailnet device allowed to reach port 8214 receives the same high-privilege routed account and workspace access.
A full host reboot was not executed; service restarts and fresh browser sessions were verified.
The router-managed marker is safe only while openai_base_url remains the exact loopback account-router path.
The real router login can expire or be revoked and must then be authorized again.
Account switching and cross-account continuity remain outside M6.6.
